data.title: Tompkins Financial 3Q 2026: Revenue $89.9M, EPS $2— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Tompkins Financial Corp. reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $89.9 million, up 2.9% from $87.4 million a year earlier, while net income increased 21% to $28.7 million and diluted EPS rose 21.2% to $2. Stronger net interest income was the primary earnings driver.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $89.9M, compared with $87.4M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 2.9%.
  • Net income was $28.7M, compared with $23.7M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 21.0%.
  • Diluted EPS was $2.00, compared with $1.65 in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 21.2%.

Business Highlights

  • Average loans grew 6.9% in the quarter, while improved asset yields and lower funding costs helped lift net interest margin to 3.65%.
  • Wealth management fees increased 6.8%; managed and advised assets reached $3.1 billion, up 3.1% year over year.
  • The sale of the insurance agency ended the company’s insurance operations, leaving banking and wealth management as its two business segments.
  • The company continues to emphasize personalized service and digital access amid competition from fintechs and alternative payment providers.

data.title: RBLX Stock Heads For Worst Day Since July As Q4 Outlook Disappoints — Analyst Flags Monetization Risks
data.description:
Key points:
  • Roblox Daily active users dropped 9% to 138 million, and engagement hours fell 15% year over year.
  • Roblox guided for a Q4 adjusted EBITDA loss of $10 million to $70 million and negative free cash flow of up to $190 million.
  • Freedom Capital bucked the trend and raised its target on RBLX as the company’s guidance beat its expectations.

Roblox (RBLX) shares plunged about 20% on Friday, putting the stock on track for its worst single-day decline since July, after the gaming platform reported weaker user engagement and issued a disappointing outlook for fourth-quarter bookings.

The sell-off came despite Roblox beating third-quarter revenue and bookings estimates, even as its fourth-quarter forecast indicated a 10% to 15% year-over-year decline in bookings. The company’s daily active users also fell 9% to 138 million.

At the time of this writing, RBLX stock was down around 20% and was among the trending tickers on Stocktwits.

Roblox Q4 Outlook Disappoints

Roblox reported third-quarter revenue of $1.57 billion, up 16% year over year, while bookings declined 12% to $1.70 billion. Its net loss narrowed to $230 million from $258 million a year earlier.

Roblox reported nearly 34 billion hours of engagement in the third quarter, down 15% year over year but up 17% from the previous quarter. The company said the annual decline reflected difficult comparisons with growth recorded in 2025.

For the fourth quarter, Roblox projected bookings of $1.89 billion to $2 billion, below analysts' expectations of approximately $2.01 billion.

The company also forecast an adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) loss of $10 million to $70 million, alongside negative free cash flow of $105 million to $190 million.

Analyst Flags Monetization, Growth Concerns

According to TheFly, Morgan Stanley lowered its price target to $50 from $55 but maintained an ‘Overweight’ rating on RBLX, saying that fourth-quarter guidance disappointed expectations for a recovery in bookings. The firm, however, remained optimistic about user growth and Roblox's product pipeline.

Roth Capital cut its target to $54 while maintaining a ‘Buy’ rating, warning that near-term headwinds could persist for another two to three quarters. However, the firm expects new initiatives to broaden Roblox's audience and improve monetization.

Wedbush also lowered its target, citing user growth in lower-monetizing regions and among younger players. The firm highlighted 18% year-over-year growth in U.S. users aged 18 and older.

UBS also cut its target, citing uncertainty around user trends, the impact of Grand Theft Auto VI, and operating leverage heading into 2027. Freedom Capital was the exception, raising its target after Roblox's guidance exceeded the firm's expectations.

Retail Investors’ Sentiment Around RBLX Stock

On Stocktwits, retail investors’ sentiment around RBLX stock flipped to ‘bearish’ territory amid high user message volume.

So far in 2026, RBLX shares have plunged over 48%. By comparison, the Vanguard Communication Services ETF (VOX), which holds the stock, has fallen nearly 11% over the same period.

data.title: Binance Hacked: CFTC Chair Says Blockchain Gives ‘A Very Good Shot’ At Tracing Stolen Funds
data.description:
Key points:
  • Selig said the blockchain could give investigators more ability to track stolen funds than they would have in a conventional bank robbery.
  • He acknowledged that hackers could use mixing services such as Tornado Cash to make funds harder to trace, but said blockchain records can still help investigators follow the money.
  • He said the CFTC wants to offer exchanges a route to register federally and become subject to cybersecurity safeguards.

Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chairman Michael Selig said on Friday that the public record of blockchain transactions gives investigators a strong chance of tracing the funds stolen in the Binance hack.

“I do believe that the blockchain gives us a very good shot,” Selig said in an interview on CNBC. His comments come after Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, was hacked on Thursday night, with losses amounting to around $6.34 billion.

Selig said the blockchain’s transaction history could help investigators follow the stolen funds, even if the attackers moved them through services designed to obscure their origins. “But I do believe the blockchain gives us a lot more ability to track this sort of stuff than, for example, if we had a bank robbery,” he said.

Selig added that the CFTC would work with law enforcement to assist with the investigation.

Binance Hack Renews CFTC Push For Crypto Oversight

Selig said the breach reinforced the CFTC’s case for bringing crypto trading venues under federal oversight, particularly offshore exchanges that operate without the safeguards required in U.S. financial markets.

“Well, this proves our exact point in proposing regulations for crypto markets earlier this month,” he said. “The real issue here is that these are unregulated offshore exchanges, and they don’t have the same sorts of safeguards that we have in our financial markets here in the U.S.”

Selig said the agency wants to offer exchanges a path to register with the CFTC, which would subject them to cybersecurity requirements similar to those in U.S. financial markets.

“We want to offer a federal option to these exchanges to come and register with the CFTC, and they would be subject to the same sorts of cybersecurity safeguards that we have in our markets today,” he said.

Blockchain Records Could Help Trace Stolen Funds

Selig said the attack on Binance targeted systems surrounding the blockchain rather than the blockchain itself. However, he noted that stolen cryptocurrency can move quickly and that attackers may use mixing services such as Tornado Cash, which pools transactions to make the origin of funds harder to trace.

Selig said that even when such services are used, the blockchain’s transaction history can give investigators a way to follow the money. He added that the CFTC would assist law enforcement with the investigation.

“I’ve heard some allegations and rumors as to where it could have gone. So we’re of course going to work with law enforcement to assist however we can,” he said.

Bitcoin, BNB Slide After Binance Hack

The crypto market has been in a tailspin since news of the hack broke, with Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH) and Binance Coin (BNB) hitting over one-month lows. Both BNB and BTC were among the top trending crypto tickers on Stocktwits at the time of writing.

BNB’s price fell over 6% in the last 24 hours, leading losses among the top 10 cryptocurrencies by market capitalization. However, retail sentiment on Stocktwits around BNB improved to ‘bullish’ from ‘neutral’ territory over the past day while chatter rose to ‘high’ from ‘normal’ levels.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin’s price dropped as much as 4.5% to around $77,500, recuperating from a drop to around $76,400, with no change in retail sentiment, still stuck in the ‘bearish’ zone.

The overall cryptocurrency market shed as much as 5% in the last 24 hours, with its valuation dropping to $2.69 trillion. CoinGlass data showed $1.65 billion in crypto liquidations, with $1.45 billion coming from long positions that were forced to unwind.

data.title: European shares stumble at end of best month since June on AI worries
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bayer gains after winning Roundup cancer trial brought by three women
  • Universal Music rises as Q3 subscription streaming revenue improves
  • Euro zone economic growth surpasses expectations

By Avinash P and Niket Nishant

European shares dropped on Friday, hammered by a global tech selloff that shaved billions off the market values of some chip heavyweights, ending a largely strong month on a sour note.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index closed 0.36% lower at 646.75 points, despite recording its best month since June.

Results from Amazon and Intel in the US rekindled concerns about the high costs of building out AI infrastructure and prompted a pullback from technology names worldwide.

"The message from investors is becoming clearer: strong AI demand is no longer enough on its own," Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, said.

The European technology sector index (.SX8P) fell 2.75% for its worst day since July 7 and led sectoral declines. AT&S , Soitec and Technoprobe led losses on the STOXX 600, with declines ranging from 9% to 13%.

Robust earnings in Europe this quarter have offered some support to stocks, but the drop on Friday shows how quickly bullishness can evaporate if global sentiment shifts.

"The market is trying to wrestle with the equation. A huge amount of capex is being spent, relative to the timeline of a return on investment. And at the moment, they don't have an answer to that," Michael Hewson, chief analyst at MCH Market Insights, said.

GROWTH DEFIES HEADWINDS

Separately, data showed the euro zone economy grew faster than predicted last quarter, displaying exceptional resilience to headwinds from expensive energy, even as surging borrowing costs and rapid inflation cloud the outlook.

Additionally, French consumer prices rose more than expected in October, recording the highest inflation rate since December 2023.

Investors are already grappling with political unrest in the euro zone's second-largest economy, at a time when the country faces mounting pressure from elevated government debt, driving French bond yields to multi-year highs.

Universal Music Group jumped 7.89%, topping the STOXX 600, after posting a pick-up in subscription streaming revenue in the third quarter. The media sector (.SXMP) rose 1.63%.

BP rose marginally after posting third-quarter net income ahead of expectations, while German sportswear maker Puma advanced 5.59% after a quarterly sales beat.

Sanofi gained 4.71% after the French pharmaceutical firm reported third-quarter results ahead of analyst expectations and lifted its outlook.

Among other movers, Bayer gained 5.46% after winning a trial on Thursday over claims by three women that its Roundup weedkiller caused their cancer.

The European Union and Canada launched an "Alliance for the Future" following a two-day summit in Montreal in a move to tighten economic and security ties during U.S. President Trump's second term.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney told reporters on Friday that he has accepted an invitation to a meeting of EU leaders in June as part of a longer-term plan to bring both economies closer together.

Both sides said in a joint statement that they would work more closely in a broad range of areas spanning critical minerals, de-escalation in the Middle East, security, artificial intelligence and instant payment systems.

data.title: Coinbase's Profit Beat Comes With a Major Catch
data.description:
Coinbase shares fell nearly 7% in premarket trading Friday after investors looked past a headline profit beat and focused instead on weaker core revenue and plans by top executives to sell up to $2.2 billion of stock.

The crypto exchange reported third-quarter net income of $718.7 million, or $2.51 per diluted share, easily beating Wall Street expectations for a loss of about $0.15 per share.

But almost all of that profit came from a $715 million unrealized gain on Coinbase's crypto holdings, making the underlying operating picture much less impressive.

Core trading activity weakened sharply.

Total revenue fell 35% year over year to $1.22 billion, while transaction revenue dropped 44% to $590 million. Consumer spot trading volume sank 59%, and operating income from the exchange business fell to $61.7 million from $480.5 million a year earlier.

There were some bright spots.

CEO Brian Armstrong said prediction markets have now surpassed $200 million in annualized revenue, helping offset part of the weakness in spot trading.

Still, insider selling plans added another layer of pressure.

Armstrong, co-founder Fred Ehrsam and President Emilie Choi have filed Rule 10b5-1 plans covering up to 13.6 million shares over roughly 14 months, worth about $2.2 billion at Thursday's closing price. That represents around 6% of Coinbase's Class A shares.

Armstrong alone plans to sell up to 8.17 million shares, more than double the size of his prior plan. The company still has about $1.96 billion of authorized share repurchases available.

Investor Takeaway

I think the biggest issue here is that Coinbase's headline profit looks much stronger than the underlying business.

The company made more than $700 million, but almost all of that came from a mark-to-market crypto gain rather than the exchange itself.

That matters because transaction revenue is still the clearest read on Coinbase's core trading economics, and a 44% decline is difficult to ignore.

The insider-sale plans make the setup even more sensitive because they introduce the possibility of meaningful additional share supply while the stock is already well below its 52-week high.

For investors, the key things to watch are spot trading volumes, transaction revenue, prediction-market growth, insider Form 4 filings, and whether the company uses its buyback authorization aggressively enough to offset new supply.

Coinbase beat on profit.

But the quality of that profit is the real story.

data.title: Quess Corp Q2 Results: Net profit jumps 45% on staffing growth; declares ₹5 dividend
data.description:
Staffing and workforce solutions provider Quess Corp Ltd on Friday (October 30) reported a 44.9% year-on-year increase in net profit to ₹75 crore for the second quarter of FY27, compared with ₹52 crore in the year-ago period.

Revenue rose 14.7% to ₹4,396 crore from ₹3,832 crore, while earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 11.6% to ₹86 crore from ₹77 crore. EBITDA margin remained flat at 2%.

The company declared an interim dividend of ₹5 per equity share, representing 50% of the face value of ₹10 per share, for FY27. November 6, 2026, has been fixed as the record date for determining shareholder eligibility. The dividend will be paid on or before November 20, 2026.

Quess Corp reported net cash of ₹471 crore and its highest-ever quarterly cash collection of more than ₹5,000 crore.

H1 FY27 Performance

For the first half of FY27, revenue stood at ₹8,578 crore, up 15% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA increased 22% to ₹178 crore, with the margin improving by 12 basis points year-on-year. Profit after tax (PAT) rose 53% to ₹157 crore, with earnings per share (EPS) at ₹10.4.

Return on equity (ROE) expanded to 25% from 20% in FY26, based on trailing 12-month PAT.

Q2 Segmental Performance

The General Staffing business reported revenue of ₹3,823 crore and EBITDA of ₹57 crore during the quarter. Its headcount stood at 490,000, with more than 20,000 additions. The business added 116 new contracts during the quarter.

The construction vertical's EBITDA nearly doubled year-on-year, with double-digit margins.

In Professional Staffing, margins stood at around 11%. Global Capability Centres (GCCs) contributed 71% of both headcount and revenue, with Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI) and CRT emerging as the leading growth verticals. The business added 27 new contracts.

Overseas Business

Quess Corp's overseas business added 33 new contracts and reported double-digit growth in both revenue and EBITDA.

The Middle East business maintained strong margins despite flat sequential revenue growth amid the geopolitical crisis. Singapore added eight new contracts, while Malaysia recorded 50% year-on-year revenue growth.

The Philippines business reported 15% year-on-year revenue growth, with a net margin of 10.5%.

Lohit Bhatia, ED and Group CEO, said, "We are pleased to report a good result for Q2, with revenue growing by 15% YoY to ₹4,396 crore and adj. EBITDA rising by 20% YoY to ₹92 crore. Our PAT and EPS grew 44% YoY, reaching ₹75 crore and ₹5, respectively, while delivering a ROE of 25%.

The Board has approved an interim dividend of ₹5 per share, reaffirming our commitment to creating sustainable value for our shareholders. This quarter’s performance was marked by a significant milestone as our headcount crossed 500k, driven largely by headcount additions of over 20k in our General Staffing business.

The segment delivered robust performance, adding 116 new client logos and achieving 15% YoY revenue growth and 23% YoY EBITDA growth, positioning us strongly for the quarters ahead. Professional Staffing recorded 13% YoY revenue growth, supported by sustained hiring demand from Global Capability Centres (GCCs).

Despite geopolitical challenges in the Middle East, our Overseas Business maintained momentum, delivering 10% YoY revenue growth and 23% YoY EBITDA growth.
